key_insight: Clinical System One (CS1), a 4-billion-parameter model, makes fast, probability-scored judgments from clinical records while a generalist language model formulates questions and synthesizes evidence.
clinical_relevance: This division of labor could make population-scale record review and clinical-trial candidate screening more efficient.
method: Trained on 12.4 million question–answer pairs from 3.6 million patients across a multi-hospital health system.
Answers multiple typed questions in one forward pass without task-specific retraining, with probabilities to support routing uncertain cases to human review.
Pairs with a language-model agent for cited patient-history answers and trial-eligibility screening.
evidence_signal: On 963,408 held-out patients, CS1 outperformed open decision models up to 27B parameters on 13 of 14 independently scored tasks; across 21 external datasets, aggregate performance approached the strongest tested 27B model with 6.4× faster inference in a matched workload.
watch_item: Retrospective benchmark results do not establish clinical benefit; prospective validation and locally calibrated human-review thresholds are needed before deployment.
paper_title: A general-purpose System One decision model for clinical records
